solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Firm hold file on origin of grievance

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of grievance is used

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file for wood or metal

explanation.surface: Someone takes a file in hand, and the grip is the root of their complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: the G from 'origin of grievance' comes before the file, though the clue names the file first.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasp is a firm grip on something, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Serious bill in front of one — no good pulling faces

indicators.note: says the bill's letters come just before the letter for one

parts.note: grim means stern or serious
AC is short for account, a bill
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Faced with a heavy bill and no use to anyone, someone pulls faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimacing is twisting the face in disgust or pain, which is pulling faces.

clue.text: Cooking and eating custard all come before fruit

definitions.text: Cooking and eating custard all come before fruit

parts.words: Cooking and eating custard all come before fruit
parts.note: cooking, eating and custard each make a named fruit when placed in front of the same five-letter fruit word

explanation.surface: A recipe step: the custard gets cooked and eaten before the fruit course.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Cooking', 'eating' and 'custard' as words placed in front of the answer: a cooking one, an eating one and a custard one are all kinds of this fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit described is the one that comes in cooking, eating and custard varieties.

clue.text: Collapse near top and put hand down

indicators.note: a collapse breaks a structure apart, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Something near the top caves in and a person lowers their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collapse' rearranges the seven letters of NEAR TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronate is to turn the hand so the palm faces down, a technical anatomy term.

clue.text: Offender's terrible crimes — a case of neglect

indicators.note: terrible crimes are badly mangled ones, telling us to rearrange the letters
the case of a word is its outside, so take the first and last letters of neglect

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer has committed dreadful crimes, chiefly a matter of neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges CRIMES into MISCRE; the 's of Offender's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, a person who breaks the law or rules.

clue.text: Young lady requiring chaps to accept assistance

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: chaps are men
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: A young woman needs some men to take on help.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an old word for a girl or unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Wholesale gin for distribution by lottery

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two parts sit next to each other

parts.note: a sweep, short for sweepstake, is a lottery

indicators.note: distributing things scatters them, so the letters of gin are reordered

explanation.surface: Bulk gin is handed out by drawing lots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for distribution' rearranges GIN to ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping changes are wholesale ones, wide-ranging and indiscriminate.

clue.text: Italian church court

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, from Rome
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A court belonging to an Italian church.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, and to romance them means the same.

clue.text: Tavern due for renovation is a risky undertaking

indicators.note: renovating a building reworks it, signalling that these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Doing up a pub that is overdue for a refit is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for renovation' rearranges TAVERN DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is an exciting, hazardous enterprise, so a risky undertaking.

clue.text: Subject putting edge into disheartened theatre

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside
with the heart taken out, leaving only the outer letters of theatre

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A subject is introduced at the edge of a theatre that has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' means the middle of theatre is removed, leaving its two outer letters to hold the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a talk, work or piece of writing.

clue.text: Make do — one's better outside

indicators.note: says the word for better wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
one is I, and the 's adds S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone getting by tells themselves they are better off outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to make do with whatever is to hand.

clue.text: Propose to take in one film

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: to move a motion is to propose it
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone proposes taking a date to see a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is a film, the American word for it.

clue.text: Hailstorm that's normal

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A hailstorm that is perfectly ordinary weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hailstorm' must be split into Hail and storm; read as one weather word it hides both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical or normal, the usual standard.

clue.text: Change includes a new act of atonement

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside

parts.note: pence are loose coins, small change

explanation.surface: Some loose coins contribute to a fresh act of making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: A penance is a punishment taken on willingly to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Part of foot — measure part of foot

parts.note: an inch, IN, is part of a foot as a length of twelve inches
a step is a measure, as in taking steps or measures

explanation.surface: A doctor names a bit of the foot and then measures a bit of the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses two kinds of foot: the body part in the definition and the twelve-inch length in the wordplay. The charade is in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched middle part of the human foot.

clue.text: Fencer's second angry exchange with valet

parts.note: to have words is to quarrel, so words means an angry exchange
a man is a manservant, a valet

explanation.surface: A fencing contest's second bout descends into a row with a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Fencer's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman is someone skilled with a sword, as a fencer is.

clue.text: Lacking confidence in organising rescue

indicators.note: organising things arranges them differently, so the letters of rescue are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A person feels unsure while running a rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of the surface reads as a link word, but it is a piece of the answer as written; 'organising' rearranges the rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure describes someone unsure of themselves, lacking self-assurance.

clue.text: Londoner's objective during religious festival

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it

parts.note: Easter is the Christian festival of the Resurrection
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A Londoner reveals their goal for the Easter holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: An EAST-ENDER comes from the East End, the traditionally working-class district of east London. The 's of Londoner's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An East Ender is a native of the East End of London, so a kind of Londoner.

clue.text: Promote a new source of fuel

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means a rearranged one

explanation.surface: An advertising push for a brand-new fuel source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PROMOTE A.
explanation.definitionFit: A peat moor is boggy upland where peat is cut and dried to burn as fuel.

clue.text: Key deficit links topless magazines

parts.note: G is a musical key
a loss is a deficit

indicators.note: with the top cut off, so the first letter goes from the word for links

parts.note: ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: A shortfall connects up with saucy topless magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the T from TIES to leave IES; the surface tempts a racier reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossies are magazines printed on shiny, high-quality paper.

clue.text: Report supporting female's affair

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, after the other

parts.note: she is a female, the pronoun for a woman
a bang is a loud report, as of a gun

explanation.surface: A news report backs up a woman's love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEBANG, as in 'the whole shebang', means the whole business or affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebang is an affair or matter, used chiefly in the phrase the whole shebang.

clue.text: Time invested in top sportsmen and horses

indicators.note: something invested in a venture is put into it

parts.note: seeds are top-ranked players in a tennis tournament

explanation.surface: Time is put into elite athletes and their racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeds is a poetic word for horses, especially riding horses.

clue.text: Examine graduate on new agreement on weapons

parts.note: to test is to examine
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate is assessed on a new arms treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: A test ban is a treaty forbidding the testing of nuclear weapons.

clue.text: Composer who was bad as ever?

indicators.note: bad letters are spoilt ones, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer whose work was as awful as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges AS EVER; Edgard Varèse was a French-born modernist composer, and the question mark admits the slur is unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varèse was an avant-garde twentieth-century composer.

clue.text: Money owed by poor society girl before start of term

indicators.note: puts the society girl's letters in front of the last piece

parts.note: bad means poor in quality
a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hard-up debutante runs up money owed before term begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad debt is money owed that will never be repaid.

clue.text: Titled lady to plead with show of hesitation

parts.note: to beg is to plead
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A noblewoman stammers as she pleads.
explanation.walkthrough: A begum is a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Begum is a title of rank for a Muslim noblewoman in India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Mollify idiot with salary, say

indicators.note: say tells us the result is spoken, matching only by its sound

parts.note: an ass is an idiot and a wage is a salary, so together they give ASS WAGE

explanation.surface: Calm down a fool by paying them.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the two pieces run together as a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or calm feelings, so to mollify.

clue.text: Prize for a raffle is raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: a draw is a raffle

explanation.surface: Money is raised by holding a raffle with a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is raised' turns DRAW upwards to WARD in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given for achievement.

clue.text: Girl from good novel by Jane Austen

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A girl taken from an excellent Jane Austen novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemma is a girl's name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Managing director is too enthusiastic!

definitions.meaning: a managing director sits above, or is placed over, the board of directors
going too far, carried away with excitement

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer 4,5 to read the first sense: the managing director's place is in charge of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Going overboard means being excessively enthusiastic, an idiom.

clue.text: People grow old and, oddly, raise animals

parts.note: men means people
to age is to grow old

indicators.note: taking the odd letters, first, third and fifth, of raise

explanation.surface: People age and, strangely, take to rearing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for show.

clue.text: Free article being rejected is a low point

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: to rid is to free
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A free item that keeps being turned down hits rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rejected' turns RIDAN backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the opposite of the zenith.
